terms.gloss: look hard at, stare at, gaze at
evidence: Hor. Epod. 5.9: quid, ut noverca, mē intuēris? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The plain classical word for fixing one’s eyes on someone or something, with the accusative. It need not be rude: it is also to look at with attention or admiration, and of the mind, to consider (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: why do you stare at me like a stepmother?

phrases.latin: nōndum loquēbātur et intuēbātur pallidus amārō aspectū conlactāneum suum
phrases.english: he could not talk yet, and he stared, pale and with a bitter look, at the baby who shared his nurse
Why are you staring at him? It isn’t nice.
